title: ～たほうがいい — “you had better ～”
summary: Used to advise someone that a certain action is best. It follows the ta-form of a verb. The negative form advises against an action.

patterns.form: 動詞ない形＋ほうがいい
patterns.gloss: verb nai-form + ほうがいい (to advise against)

body.p: It recommends one choice over the others. 薬を飲んだほうがいいです recommends taking the medicine.
To advise against something, use the nai-form (夜は食べないほうがいいです). Do not use なかったほうがいい here.
It is clear advice, so it can feel pushy toward a superior. In that case use softer forms such as 〜といいですよ.

examples.ja: 早（はや）く寝（ね）たほうがいいです。
examples.romaji: Hayaku neta hō ga ii desu.
examples.tr: You had better go to bed early.

examples.ja: 薬（くすり）を飲（の）んだほうがいいです。
examples.romaji: Kusuri o nonda hō ga ii desu.

examples.ja: 野菜（やさい）を食（た）べたほうがいいです。
examples.romaji: Yasai o tabeta hō ga ii desu.

pitfalls: For positive advice use the ta-form. The dictionary form is mainly for comparisons.
The negative is ないほうがいい, not なかったほうがいい.
